title: Open GitHub Copilot inside your code editor
summary: Ask the editor to read a tiny file. You can find the answer in that same file.
where: Use a Mac or PC. Get Visual Studio Code from code.visualstudio.com. You need a GitHub account with Copilot access. The desktop folder and toolbar steps here take place on the computer. An iPad can hold these directions.

actions.title: Open a folder
actions.do: In Documents make a folder called AI-Editor-Practice. Start Visual Studio Code. Choose File → Open Folder and select that folder.
actions.see: Its name appears in the file list.
actions.stuck: If it shows an old project, use File → Open Folder again and choose the new folder.

actions.title: Sign in
actions.do: Point to the Copilot status icon. Choose Use AI Features or Sign in to use Copilot. Finish the GitHub sign-in in your browser, then return to Visual Studio Code.
actions.see: The editor shows Copilot as available for this account.
actions.stuck: If it offers several accounts, use the one that has Copilot access.

actions.title: Make one file
actions.do: Choose File → New Text File. Type “Queue target: 15 minutes.” Save it in the practice folder as service.txt.
actions.see: You can click service.txt in the file list and see the sentence.
actions.stuck: If it is called Untitled, choose Save As and pick the practice folder before continuing.

actions.title: Ask a question
actions.do: Open Chat in the editor. Ask “Read service.txt. What is the target and what is its unit? Leave the file alone.” Attach the file if Chat asks for it.
actions.see: The answer should say 15 minutes. You can read the same fact in the file.
actions.stuck: If it says 15 hours, ask for the exact words from the source.

roles: Read a goal in a pretend mail note.
Look up a target in a shared guide.
Check which settings an app file names.
sources: Microsoft · set up GitHub Copilot in VS Code

title: Try a code suggestion as you type
summary: The editor may offer faint words while you type. You choose whether to put those words in the file.
where: Open desktop Visual Studio Code with GitHub Copilot enabled. Use a practice folder. A file ending in .js holds JavaScript, the language in this small example.

actions.title: Start the file
actions.do: Create double.js. On the first line type // Return twice a numeric value. Press Enter. The two slashes make the line a note for readers.
actions.see: You have a new line after your note.
actions.stuck: If the file ends in .txt, save it as double.js before looking for code suggestions.

actions.title: Give it a start
actions.do: Type function doubleValue(n) { and press Enter. The n stands for the number you will give it. Pause for the suggestion.
actions.see: Dim text may appear. It is only a suggestion until you accept it.
actions.stuck: If you do not see one, check the Copilot icon. You can still type the answer in the next step.

actions.title: Choose the useful bit
actions.do: A correct answer can use return n * 2; inside the braces. Press Tab to use a matching suggestion. Press Escape to dismiss a wrong one. Type the line yourself if needed, then the closing }.
actions.see: The file now has a complete function that doubles its input.
actions.stuck: If the function has two closing braces, remove the extra one. Then save.

actions.title: Check three inputs
actions.do: In Chat ask what the saved function would return for 3, 0 and -2. Multiply each number by two on paper.
actions.see: The answers should be 6, 0 and -4.
actions.stuck: If the first answer is 5, see whether the suggestion adds 2 instead of multiplying by 2.

roles: Double small practice mail counts.
Check a simple formula used in a team tool.
Double bonus points in a game.
sources: Microsoft · set up GitHub Copilot in VS Code

title: Find what an equals sign changes
summary: Two rules look almost the same. Test three small numbers to find where they disagree.
where: Use Chat in desktop Visual Studio Code with GitHub Copilot signed in. Open a folder where you may create a practice file.

actions.title: Make the rule
actions.do: Save a file called rule.js containing this line: const isReady = count => count >= 3; The last part asks whether the count is at least three.
actions.see: The saved file shows >= with both marks.
actions.stuck: If the editor puts quotes around the whole line, remove them and save again.

actions.title: Try three numbers
actions.do: In Chat, attach rule.js or use the open file as its source. Ask “Read this rule. What happens for 2, 3 and 4? Keep the file as it is.”
actions.see: The answers are false, true, true. Three just meets the rule.
actions.stuck: If no file appears beside the prompt, add rule.js with the context control and ask again.

actions.title: Change one mark
actions.do: Remove the equals sign so the rule now uses > 3. Save it. Ask Chat for the results with the same three numbers.
actions.see: The answers now read false, false, true.
actions.stuck: If the old answer returns, tell Chat to read the saved copy again.

actions.title: Name the change
actions.do: Write the two sets of answers on paper and circle the one column that changed. Ask Chat why it changed.
actions.see: Only 3 moved from true to false. It equals 3 and does not exceed it.
actions.stuck: If the explanation focuses on 2 or 4, compare those two columns. Each stayed the same.

roles: Check when a mail alert starts.
Test a threshold on a shared form.
Check a game’s unlock rule.
sources: Microsoft · set up GitHub Copilot in VS Code

title: Ask your first question in work Copilot
summary: Read a mail notice and spot a detail it leaves out.
where: On a Mac, PC or iPad, open m365.cloud.microsoft/chat in a browser. Use your work or school account with access. You can also use the work chat in the Microsoft 365 Copilot mobile app if available.

actions.title: Check the account
actions.do: Choose Sign in if asked. Select the account that has access to the work chat. Look at the workspace label.
actions.see: You have opened the intended workspace.
actions.stuck: If the account is personal, switch accounts before using the work chat.

actions.title: Find the message box
actions.do: Choose Chat or New if needed. Tap the field where you can type a message.
actions.see: A cursor appears in the message field.
actions.stuck: If you are reading an old reply, choose New chat for this exercise.

actions.title: Ask about a notice
actions.do: Type “Sample notice: shared mailbox search resumes at 14:00 UTC. Delivery continues. Which feature is affected?” Send it.
actions.see: The answer should point to search. Mail delivery continues.
actions.stuck: If the answer says the whole service stops, ask which sentence says so.

actions.title: Check what is missing
actions.do: Ask “Who is responsible for the change? Use only the notice.” Read the sample again yourself.
actions.see: The notice gives no owner. A useful answer says so.
actions.stuck: If it supplies a name, ask for the exact words in the sample that name the owner.

roles: Read a sample mail notice.
Check what a service update actually says.
Write a help notice without making up details.
sources: Microsoft · start Copilot Chat at work

title: Check a mail summary in Outlook
summary: Compare a summary with the original messages. Watch for the difference between a proposed day and a booked day.
where: Open Outlook on your computer or mobile device with access to Copilot. You can practice with only the supplied practice messages by pasting them into work Copilot Chat.

actions.title: Find a conversation
actions.do: In Outlook, open a practice thread you are allowed to read. In the conversation controls, look for Summary by Copilot or Summarize.
actions.see: If available, this opens a short account of the thread.
actions.stuck: If the button is missing, move to the sample chat exercise.

actions.title: Read the source
actions.do: Choose a numbered reference if the summary includes one. Read the message it points to. Compare its exact words with the summary.
actions.see: You can tell whether the sentence in the summary has support.
actions.stuck: If there are no reference numbers, compare the original messages in order yourself.

actions.title: Try three messages
actions.do: In work chat paste “M1 Owner: Tuesday is booked. M2 Desk: Could we switch to Wednesday? M3 Owner: I will check.” Ask which day is firm and which is proposed.
actions.see: Tuesday is booked. Wednesday is still a request.
actions.stuck: If Wednesday is called final, ask where the owner agreed to the switch.

actions.title: Draft a question
actions.do: Ask for one line that requests the owner’s final choice. Read the draft and check its meaning.
actions.see: The draft can ask if Wednesday was approved. It makes no claim that the day already changed.
actions.stuck: If the draft announces Wednesday, ask it to phrase the line as a question.

roles: Find a confirmed mail change date.
Summarize a short project thread.
Draft a question about a planned game night.
sources: Microsoft · start Copilot Chat at work

title: Read a meeting recap in Teams
summary: Use two short meeting lines to separate an idea from an approved decision.
where: In Teams open a past practice meeting you may read. You can also open m365.cloud.microsoft/chat and use only the two lines. Meeting settings and account access affect the recap and transcript you can see.

actions.title: Open Recap
actions.do: Open the meeting chat. Select Recap and look for Copilot if your account offers it.
actions.see: The recap shows the material available for that meeting.
actions.stuck: If Recap is missing or empty, use the made-up chat exercise in step 3.

actions.title: Look at one line
actions.do: If the meeting has a transcript, find one line with a speaker and a time. A transcript is a written record of speech.
actions.see: You can trace a statement to its place in the meeting.
actions.stuck: If there is no transcript, keep any claim about what was said open.

actions.title: Check two days
actions.do: In work chat paste “10:01 Host: I propose Friday. 10:05 Owner: Monday approved.” Ask which day was proposed and which was approved. Ask for the time beside each.
actions.see: Friday is the suggestion at 10:01. Monday is the decision at 10:05.
actions.stuck: If both days look final, compare the words propose and approved.

actions.title: Ask who will do it
actions.do: Ask “Who agreed to carry out the work?” Read both sample lines before accepting the answer.
actions.see: Neither line names someone who will carry it out. Approving the day does not assign the job.
actions.stuck: If the answer chooses the owner, ask which line says the owner will do the work.

roles: Check a decision in mail support notes.
Read a Teams recap with care.
Track which game change was approved.
sources: Microsoft · start Copilot Chat at work

title: Ask Excel to check a tiny table
summary: Give Excel two numbers you can add by hand. Then change one and see whether its answer follows.
where: Open Excel with an account that offers Copilot. Start a practice workbook. If you only have work Copilot Chat, paste the same table into chat and check the math yourself.

actions.title: Fill four cells
actions.do: Type Team in A1 and Count in B1. On row 2 enter North and 4. On row 3 enter South and 7. A cell is one box in the sheet.
actions.see: Column B now has 4 and 7 in the Count column.
actions.stuck: If the numbers landed in the Team column, move them into B2 and B3.

actions.title: Ask for a formula
actions.do: Select the table and open Copilot. Ask “Which formula adds the two counts? Name the cells.” In chat, include the rows with this question.
actions.see: A suitable reply is =SUM(B2:B3). The range means B2 through B3.
actions.stuck: If it includes B4, point out that B4 is the place where the total belongs.

actions.title: Check the result
actions.do: Enter the formula in B4 and press Enter. In chat, add the two numbers on paper instead.
actions.see: The total is 11 because 4 plus 7 is 11.
actions.stuck: If B4 displays the formula as words, check that it starts with = and that the cell accepts formulas.

actions.title: Change one input
actions.do: Replace 7 with 9 in B3. Read B4 again. If working in chat, send the revised rows and ask again.
actions.see: The new total is 13.
actions.stuck: If the sheet still says 11, click B4 and look for the formula. A typed 11 cannot update itself.

roles: Add two sample mail counts.
Check totals in a shared practice sheet.
Build a simple score total.
